hints.title: Descending Value Priority
hints.text: To maximize cumulative total, prioritize elements carrying the highest positive contributions.

hints.title: Capacity Limitation
hints.text: Stop accumulating once k elements have been activated or no positive contributions remain.

hints.title: Index Sorting
hints.text: Sort element indices in descending order of value to select greedily.

hints.title: Reference Implementation
hints.text:
```python
import heapq
from typing import List

class Solution:
    def maxTotal(self, values: List[int], limits: List[int], k: int) -> int:
        # Group values by limit group/category or pair them
        # Pair (value, limit) and pick up to k elements maximizing sum
        items = sorted(zip(values, limits), key=lambda x: -x[0])
        total = 0
        used = 0
        
        # Track counts used per limit category if categorized, or take top k largest positive values
        for val, lim in items:
            if used < k and val > 0:
                total += val
                used += 1
                
        return total
```

complexity.notes: Sorts items by value descending and accumulates top k positive values.
complexity.whyNaiveFails: Checking all subset combinations of size k takes exponential time.
complexity.spaceTimeTradeoff: Uses O(N) space for index ordering.
complexity.interviewerExpectation: Sort greedily by contribution and enforce cardinality constraints.
